results.title: Breathing Poison: Toxic smoke from Agbogbloshie e-waste burning still making workers sick
results.content: Smoke from burning electronic waste at Agbogbloshie in Accra is filling the air with toxic chemicals, and researchers have long said the harmful effects are already getting into people's bodies — making them sick and, in some cases, killing them. It has been nearly two decades since clear evidence of direct human exposure to e-waste contaminants was found among workers at Agbogbloshie. In a 2012 study, urine samples from 20 male e-waste workers aged between 15 and 42 found significantly higher levels of iron, the flame-retardant antimony, and lead in the urine of the e-waste workers.

results.title: World Cup visa scandal: $26,000 paid to police on behalf of Ampofo Ankrah

results.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Starting the 2027 Strategic Planning Process
results.content: Strategic planning for 2027 should begin before the current year closes. CEOs who wait until December risk making important decisions under time pressure, relying on incomplete analysis, or carrying existing priorities into the new year without sufficient review. Starting early gives the executive team time to examine current performance, understand market developments, reassess strategic assumptions, and determine what the organization must do differently to achieve its next set of objectives.

results.title: Is Afenyo-Markin’s GH¢15 million suit a face-saving writ?
results.content: If Afenyo-Markin does not go back to court, properly, and make the process public, Ghanaians will believe Sammy Gyamfi. That is not law. That is how public trust works. You cannot file a defective writ, lose on a technicality, and then expect us to clap for you and move on. If Sammy Gyamfi has no evidence, let the court expose him. Let him be made to prove his emphatic claim to strict proof. But if he has the evidence he claims to have, then let it also come out.

results.content: Ghana’s democratic transitions rightly inspire admiration. It is therefore all the more unfortunate, and deeply worrying, that each change of government can leave committed entrepreneurs unpaid, loyal workers uncertain and promising enterprises struggling to survive.
